source.chapitre: Grammar: present, past, perfect, future tenses

activites.question: Which sentence expresses a habit (present simple)?
activites.explication: The present simple expresses habits and general truths; the present continuous expresses actions happening now.

activites.phrase: Complete (present continuous): « Look! The children ___ (play) football right now. »
activites.explication: Present continuous = be + verb-ing, for an action happening now.

activites.question: Which sentence is in the past simple?
options: He was playing when I arrived.
activites.explication: Past simple = finished action at a definite past time (yesterday).

activites.question: Choose the past continuous: an action in progress in the past.
options: I was watching TV when the phone rang.
activites.explication: Past continuous = was/were + verb-ing, for an action in progress in the past.

activites.question: Which sentence is in the present perfect?
options: I have already finished my homework.
activites.explication: Present perfect = have/has + past participle; links a past action to the present.

activites.consigne: Match each future form with its use.

paires.droite: a fixed arrangement in the near future

activites.explication: English expresses the future in several ways.

activites.consigne: Put these sentences in order from past to future.
elements: I had finished before he came. (past perfect)
ordreCorrect: I had finished before he came. (past perfect)
activites.explication: Timeline: past perfect < past simple < present perfect < future.
